PullRequest.Title: Codex: do not send workspace folders of non-file schemes as paths
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #335034

## Problem

The Codex agent host passes the `fsPath` of every workspace folder to the Codex app-server as the thread `cwd` and as `runtimeWorkspaceRoots`. This includes folders of extension-registered file systems, such as `abap:`. On Windows those paths have no drive, so Codex rejects them with "AbsolutePathBuf deserialized without a base path". On other platforms they are misread as local folders. The Copilot agent host already keeps only `file` folders.

## Change

`localWorkingDirectories` keeps only `file` folders. It is applied:
- when a chat is created, and so before a fork;
- on each send;
- to restored metadata, through `distinctWorkingDirectories`.

A workspace with no local folder falls back to the managed scratch directory, as when no folder is open.

## How it was tested

- New unit test: `workspace folders of non-file schemes are not sent to codex as paths`, run with `npx mocha test/unit/node/index.ts --delay --ui=tdd --exit --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/codex/codexPrewarmEviction.test.ts`.
  - On main (without the `codexAgent.ts` change) it fails: `/example` becomes the cwd and a workspace root.
  - On this branch it passes.
- All `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/codex/*.test.ts`: 836 passing.
- `pnpm run oxlint` on both changed files: clean.
- Not tested: a live Codex session with an extension file system on Windows.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create and prewarm a Codex chat in a local or mixed-scheme workspace, then send its first message.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Creation refreshes models when necessary and registers a deferred default-chat backing or awaits an eager secondary-chat thread/start. Deferred prewarm is off the create critical path; first send waits for any materialization, customization preparation and turn/start acknowledgement, not turn completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve customization directories and parse their files; stat secondary .agents/skills and .codex/skills candidates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Discovery visits deduplicated local roots and their matching files; secondary capability stat calls are at most 2*(K-1), issued together.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery and capability operations existed. Filtering removes non-file roots from the supplied set; local-only workspace behavior and invocation count remain unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Customization launch and capability preparation are awaited before materialization or turn submission.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Watch each shared root and initially read its .mcp.json.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial scan and watcher per distinct root shared by the file-service instance; initialized empty results are cached too. Later refreshes avoid disk reads unless forced by a watcher event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical shared discovery, negative-result caching and watcher lifetime existed; removed virtual roots reduce the set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial discovery is awaited before launch; subsequent sends normally consume initialized snapshots.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit thread/start, primary-cwd hooks/list when trusted, and turn/start to the app-server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One ordinary thread/start per materialized chat and one turn/start per message; hooks/list is primary-cwd scoped, not per root. Existing signature changes can cause bounded restart/resume preparation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These requests and synchronization already existed; the diff changes their cwd/root values, not their per-message or per-chat request count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Requests are awaited before first-message submission completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize root arrays into existing NDJSON requests and persisted metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialization per existing request or metadata update; root payload scales with K rather than all supplied schemes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same serializers were used. The new filter creates a transient linear array but removes invalid root strings from downstream payloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Request serialization precedes stdin write; normal materialized-session persistence is fire-and-forget.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N supplied workspace URIs, K distinct retained local filesystem roots, and agent/skill files under those roots. Filtering is O(N); path deduplication remains linear. Secondary capability candidates are at most 2*(K-1), not one app-server request per workspace folder.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Chat lifecycle operations use a per-chat sequencer. Materialization is coalesced per session. MCP roots refresh concurrently but serialize per shared root. Capability stats use Promise.all. Linux thread creations acquire sorted distinct root keys; other platforms and disjoint Linux roots remain unsequenced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Ready connections and in-flight connection starts are reused. Per-session materializePromise coalesces prewarm with first send. MCP discovery shares positive and empty initialized snapshots per root; workspace agent/skill scans themselves are uncached, as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: complete changed hunks, helper implementations, creation/send call paths and added request-shape tests establish the filtering and unchanged scheduling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Workspace root/file counts and actual IPC/filesystem duration are unmeasured. The extra filter allocation is linear in a normally small URI snapshot, with no demonstrated material regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: local behavior keeps existing boundary cardinality; mixed workspaces remove invalid roots and generally reduce discovery and serialization work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create and use a chat with only extension filesystem folders and no local workspace folder.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing workspaceless path supplies a managed scratch cwd. For a deferred default chat this happens during prewarm or first materialization; an eager secondary chat awaits scratch creation and thread/start before returning.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a deterministic scratch directory with recursive mkdir, retain it for the session, and remove it through existing failure/teardown ownership.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One creation per backing that lacks a cwd; subsequent messages reuse session.workingDirectory. Removal follows existing owned-resource cleanup, not every send.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A non-file first folder previously supplied its fsPath instead of using scratch. Empty workspaces already used this same scratch path. The diff newly routes virtual-only workspaces into that established fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: mkdir is awaited before thread/start; cleanup is on failure, abandonment or disposal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn and initialize the native Codex app-server when no ready connection exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared in-flight process startup per agent connection generation; warm messages reuse the process, not one process per folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Virtual-workspace chat requests already required this same app-server; filtering does not create additional process startups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold process initialization is awaited before requests can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download and extract the native SDK only when no configured override or completed cached SDK exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One download per missing package/version/target cache directory, coalesced within the downloader; completed cache hits avoid network and recent failures are latched.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: SDK resolution/download was already required for Codex initialization independently of workspace scheme.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A genuinely cold SDK blocks shared connection startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: On first send, probe the scratch cwd with git rev-parse for optional baseline capture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cold root probe for this scratch path; repository-root lookups coalesce per URI and cache both repository roots and non-repository results in a bounded LRU. A normal scratch directory has no repository to checkpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A non-file URI was rejected by getRepositoryRoot without a subprocess; no-workspace scratch chats already performed the same optional probe.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Codex starts baseline capture without awaiting it, so this probe is off the send critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N non-file URIs are filtered to zero; one managed scratch path per backing owner. Startup cost depends on SDK availability, not N.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing shared connection promise prevents startup fan-out; per-session materializePromise prevents duplicate scratch/materialization work. Scratch paths are distinct per owner; Linux thread creation locking remains per intersecting root set. Baseline capture is sequenced per session and runs off the send critical path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The scratch cwd is stored on the session and reused. Connection startup is coalesced and warm connections reused. SDK positive cache is version/target keyed with a completion sentinel, in-flight downloads are shared, and recent non-cancellation failures are negatively cached. Normal scratch customization roots are suppressed by _customizationWorkingDirectories.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new filter, existing missing-cwd branches, mkdir implementation, startup coalescing and baseline Git guards were read.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No live extension-filesystem or Windows profiling was performed. mkdir/startup durations depend on the host and SDK cache; the new scratch-specific work is bounded per session.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: this is a bounded reuse of the established workspaceless behavior needed to replace unusable paths, not a repeated startup or retained-resource mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send successive messages while workspace folders are replaced, reduced, removed or become virtual-only.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Send filters the snapshot, adopts a different local cwd only through existing prewarm rules, refreshes MCP discovery, reconciles customization signatures, and awaits one turn/start acknowledgement. Already materialized threads retain their process cwd.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh cached MCP snapshots and discover customization files for the current effective roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: MCP disk reads are cold per shared root or watcher-forced; root-set replacement disposes prior discovery references. Existing customization scans run during send preparation. After an explicit empty snapshot, discovery can use the single existing cwd instead of zero customization roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: MCP discovery already fell back to session.workingDirectory when the snapshot was empty. Workspace customization discovery previously saw an explicit empty array; the new undefined fallback intentionally gives it the existing cwd, matching ordinary single-root behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery needed for launch signatures is awaited before turn submission.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Unsubscribe/recreate stale prewarm when adopting a genuinely different local cwd, resume when launch signatures change, and submit turn/start with replacement runtime roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One turn/start per ordinary message, not per root. An actual launch-signature transition may require the existing unsubscribe/resume or restart path; stable subsequent snapshots do not inherently force repeated resumes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These lifecycle requests already existed. Non-file first roots previously could trigger stale-prewarm adoption; filtering now avoids that invalid cwd change. Empty local snapshots intentionally retain the thread cwd and replace secondary roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Prewarm adoption and any required launch reload precede turn/start.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Current URI snapshot N, retained distinct roots K, messages M, and customization files in retained roots. An empty local snapshot falls back to the one existing cwd rather than accumulating historical roots.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Send preparation is sequential along its awaits; MCP root scans are shared/serialized per root and concurrent across roots. Materialization and resume use per-session promises. Linux start/resume/fork locking is per intersecting root set; turn/start is one request containing the entire root array.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: MCP roots are signature-keyed, shared and initialized even for empty results. Root-set changes dispose prior entries. Materialized customization/MCP signatures avoid reload when stable; customization filesystem scanning itself remains uncached. Undefined legacy snapshots preserve restored roots, while explicit empty snapshots replace them.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed empty-snapshot assignment, customization fallback, cached MCP implementation, prewarm adoption and reload signature checks were traced; added tests corroborate one existing-thread turn request and cwd-only roots after removal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: File counts under the retained cwd and cost of a one-time signature transition are unmeasured. No evidence shows new collection fan-out, repeated reloads or unbounded retained roots.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence actionable performance bug: the changed fallback intentionally retains the thread's cwd, with bounded single-root discovery and existing signature-based reload behavior. Additional transient filtering is not a demonstrated material regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore a saved Codex chat or read its metadata in a session listing.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Passive listing can answer from discovery/registry metadata; live metadata reads answer from memory. Explicit cold restore reads authoritative thread metadata and the persisted overlay, filters restored working directories, and registers a resumable entry. Its next send awaits thread/resume.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open an existing session database and read the persisted overlay fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Six metadata-field reads per overlay read when a database exists; cold restore can read the overlay during thread resolution and again during entry reconstruction. Filtering is after existing reads and adds no database calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same overlay calls, reference disposal and field reads; distinctWorkingDirectories previously normalized all supplied schemes and now excludes non-file schemes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold restore awaits the overlay reads; warm live metadata paths bypass them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read thread metadata without turns and resume the thread on its first restored send.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Ordinary successful cold metadata read issues one thread/read; first restored send issues the existing resume operation. Passive discovered/live rows avoid thread/read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same metadata/read and resume scheduling, with no new app-server request per restored root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold restore waits for thread/read; resume is on the later send path, not newly made eager by filtering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Saved chats C, root URIs per saved chat N, and retained local roots K. Ordinary metadata restore uses includeTurns=false rather than reading the full conversation history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cold session reads use the existing global limiter of eight; reads of already-live sessions bypass that cold limiter. Resume requests coalesce per session and use existing Linux per-root creation locking.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Discovery metadata and live runtime metadata provide warm fast paths. Filtering does not alter discovery cache keys or allocate extra runtimes. Persisted URI filtering is transient, with no new retained map or negative-cache invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: metadata fast paths, cold limiter, includeTurns=false, overlay reads and restored-entry filtering were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Saved chat/root counts and database/IPC timing are unknown. No altered call frequency, history loading or retention was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: this hunk is a linear filter after unchanged metadata boundaries and normally shrinks restored root sets.

Scenarios.Scenario: Fork an existing Codex chat, including one created with only virtual workspace folders.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Fork creation resolves the source binding, resumes the source if required, reads authoritative source turns, resolves the requested fork boundary, optionally prepares/copies managed scratch, and awaits thread/fork. The fork's first send later resumes its backing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read source metadata/history, submit one thread/fork, and optionally read the fork to seed supplied turn-id mappings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One source thread/read plus existing sequential history pages for paginated threads, one thread/fork, and an optional forked-history read when turnIdMapping exists; roots are supplied in one request rather than separate forks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical source read, pagination, fork and mapping logic; filtering only changes the inherited effective root set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Source history and fork request are awaited by creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a managed scratch cwd and recursively copy the source scratch when the source owns one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One mkdir and one recursive copy per managed fork; copy work scales with B, not workspace folder count. Failed preparation removes the owned target through existing cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The managed-fork copy path already existed for workspaceless chats. The diff makes virtual-only newly created sources workspaceless, so later forks of those sources can enter this existing behavior; local sources still do not copy their workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The managed copy completes before thread/fork.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Source history H and page count P, inherited distinct local roots K, and managed scratch file count/bytes B when the source owns scratch. Root filtering does not increase H or P.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Source reads/history pages complete in order. Fork creation is sequenced per chat, and Linux thread/fork shares the sorted intersecting-root sequencer. Recursive scratch copy is one awaited operation per managed fork; the diff adds no copy loop or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Live source bindings and working directories are reused. The existing read and history handling is unchanged. Managed scratch is an owned per-backing resource, not an accumulating cache; source and fork each retain their own explicit path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call-path and ownership: source resolution, history paging, inherited root filtering, managed scratch copy and error cleanup were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual scratch size and fork history length are unmeasured. Large managed scratch can make the existing copy expensive, but no new multiplicity or avoidable copying was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: filtering narrows inherited roots and preserves the existing semantics required for independent forks of workspaceless sources.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass against base b18f25f0f5d5c0d7f55bbaaa547410fdd5a40a40 and head 9735a3f4510531409ad4bc5c60f91be79ebbce91. Inspected the complete two-file inventory, all six changed hunks, added tests, and relevant creation/send/restore/fork helpers and boundary/cache implementations. No high-confidence diff-introduced actionable performance regressions found. The PR principally filters invalid URI schemes, adds bounded scratch fallback reachability and retains existing scheduling/coalescing/cleanup. No regression-fix learning signal submitted: removal of invalid paths is demonstrated as a functional fix, not independently established as a concrete old performance regression. Static review; no measured timing or live Codex execution.
